lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Put Crestway before Lakeview in Experience while keeping Greenleaf first.
items.because: The current order places an older job ahead of a newer one, making the work history harder to follow.

items.says: Move Experience above Education.
items.because: Several years of relevant experience are the strongest evidence.

items.says: Make sure the profile link is a complete, working URL in the document.
items.because: The pasted text does not establish whether the link works.

items.says: Keep the focus on delivery volume and retain payment handling only if relevant to the target role.
items.because: Delivery volume is more relevant to an operations or supply-chain target.

items.says: Consider giving routine stocking and labeling less space.
items.because: They may take space away from stronger analytical accomplishments.

items.says: Specify what changed in the pick-path work and how shift leads used the reports.
items.because: The work and its operational value need more detail.

items.says: Clarify what the three-day measure represents and how the before-and-after periods were measured.
Clarify the comparison period or how average dock wait was measured.
items.because: That would make the reduction easier to interpret.

items.says: Separate the inventory-accuracy achievement from the other duties or remove lower-priority tasks.
items.because: Combining them makes it difficult to tell what drove the accuracy improvement.

items.says: Clarify the period and basis for the 91% to 98.5% accuracy measurement.
Make clear whether night-shift supervision was a formal assignment or coverage.
Clarify that forklift certification scheduling means administering the schedule, if that is what you did.
items.because: The wording could imply you certified operators.

items.says: Clarify the timeframe and how stockouts and inventory reduction were measured.
Be precise about your role in developing or implementing the forecast model.
Present the inventory reduction and service improvement as related results only if the evidence supports that connection.
Clarify the freight-cost comparison period or baseline and check that the 15% is like-for-like.
items.because: Unrelated volume or rate shifts could affect the comparison.

items.says: Add a supported outcome or consider whether the bullet adds distinct value.
items.because: It currently gives no outcome and sits alongside the forecasting bullet.

items.says: Retain “every SKU” only if that scope is accurate.
Explain what changed because buyers used the scorecard.
items.because: The result is unclear.

items.says: Explain how the five suppliers were identified as least reliable.
items.because: Otherwise the label can seem subjective.

items.says: The stated OEE of 112% is above the generally interpreted 0–100% scale.
items.because: It may indicate a baseline, ideal cycle time, or calculation issue.

items.says: Tie the changeover and micro-stop changes to the OEE result only if that relationship is supported.
Recheck the lead-time, throughput, and WIP figures, definitions, and measurement periods together.
items.because: Halving lead time while doubling WIP with constant throughput can sound contradictory.

items.says: Explain the operational trade-off or omit the WIP detail.
items.because: Doubling WIP could undercut the impression created by shorter lead time.

items.says: Reconsider “to keep pickers busy.”
items.because: It may sound like inventory was increased to occupy labor rather than improve the process.

items.says: Clarify whether the 85 stops represent a typical day or a particular sample.
items.because: The scope affects how readers interpret the 18% reduction.

items.says: Make clear that planned and current routes were compared under equivalent constraints.
items.because: Service and routing constraints affect the mileage comparison.

items.says: Clarify what “within 5%” compares and over which routes or trips.
Keep the drive-time validation distinct from proof of realized mileage savings.
items.because: The comparison with logs does not establish realized savings.

items.says: Clarify whether the pilot achieved any measured mileage savings.
items.because: The text establishes that routes were piloted, not that they realized the projected savings.

items.says: Clarify the grocer relationship or anonymization and confirm the operational details can be shared.
Give the recommendation bullet a distinct purpose or remove it.
items.because: It is too general beside the more specific bullets that follow.

items.says: Clarify how the one-day improvement was measured.
Clarify your contribution to the intake change.
items.because: The project identifies you as one of four people, so the bullet should not imply you alone delivered the result.

items.says: Resolve the near-identical scope and results in this bullet and Crestway’s forecasting bullet.
items.because: The overlap raises a credibility question about whether the projects and results are distinct.

items.says: Make clear what you personally contributed to the forecast.
items.because: You were part of a four-person team.

items.says: Make the specific use of Excel and Python more visible.
items.because: Their use is not always apparent from the descriptions.

items.says: Check whether each listed method is clearly demonstrated elsewhere in the résumé.
